title: Payroll funding, payroll journal entries and bank withdrawals by pay period
prompt: Reconcile payroll funding, payroll journal entries and actual bank withdrawals by pay period. Explain differences caused by deposits, fees or timing.
keywords: last pay date (period rule stand-in: business_day)
comment: Trigger period rule: the library has no last_pay_date rule yet, so business_day stands in; the pay period itself comes from the payCalendar setup answer and the register dates. Runs on the payroll.pay_run event or on request.

setup.q: Which ledger account is the payroll clearing or payroll funding account?
What is the pay calendar (frequency, pay dates, the lag between period end and pay date)?

inputs.name: Payroll gross-to-net report for the pay period
Payroll funding report for the pay period
Bank statement covering the pay date

steps: resolve the pay period and pay date from the pay calendar and the register
run column_map over the gross-to-net and funding reports (headers never positions) and save the mapping to data/payroll-funding-columns.json
pull the payroll journal entries and the payroll clearing account ledger for the period
pull the bank withdrawals on and around the pay date from the connection or statement

tie funding report total to the payroll journal entry and to the bank withdrawals; classify each difference as a deposit (direct deposit returned or held), a fee (provider fee billed with payroll) or timing (withdrawal in the next period)
write the workbook with totals only; no employee-level pay in any sheet

done.text: The gross-to-net and funding report columns were mapped by header with no ambiguous or missing required column
Every exception row cites the report line, the journal entry id or the bank transaction id
payroll-funding-reconciliation.xlsx opens with Exceptions first (count and total on the first rows), a Tie-out block whose Difference is 0.00, and no internal plumbing words
Each difference is classified as deposit, fee or timing with the figure on both sides; a difference that fits none is listed as unexplained, not forced into a class
The deliverable carries totals only: no employee name, pay, deduction or identifier leaves the source reports
